paragraphs.title: Waiting for Salvation and Being Set on Firm Ground

answers: The LORD
His enemies
The congregation
easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “I waited patiently for the LORD.”
easy.q: Whom did the speaker patiently wait for?

answers: An horrible pit and miry clay
A palace and a city
A desert and a river
easy.explanation: The LORD brought him “out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay.”
easy.q: From what did the LORD bring up the speaker?

answers: A new song
A commandment
A complaint
easy.explanation: The LORD put “a new song” in his mouth, even praise unto God.
easy.q: What did the LORD put in the speaker’s mouth?

answers: Waiting, being heard and rescued, then being established
Singing, fleeing, then hiding
Falling, boasting, then refusing help
medium.explanation: The speaker waits for the LORD, the LORD hears his cry, rescues him, and establishes his steps.
medium.q: What sequence is described in these verses?

answers: A place of severe trouble
A place of celebration
A peaceful resting place
medium.explanation: The pit and miry clay picture danger, distress, and instability.
medium.q: What does the phrase “an horrible pit” suggest?

answers: They see, fear, and trust in the LORD
They become proud and self-reliant
They turn aside to lies
medium.explanation: Many shall see it, fear, and trust in the LORD.
medium.q: What effect does the new song have on many people?

answers: A movement from instability to security
A movement from joy to sorrow
A movement from speech to silence
challenge.explanation: The speaker is lifted from the miry clay and placed upon a rock, showing rescue and stability.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the pit to the rock symbolize?

answers: Trusting the LORD is opposed to relying on the proud and those who turn aside to lies
Trusting the LORD depends on the strength of the crowd
Trusting the LORD requires believing falsehood
challenge.explanation: The blessed person makes the LORD his trust and does not respect the proud or those who turn aside to lies.
challenge.q: How is trusting the LORD contrasted with the warning in verse 4?

answers: It becomes a new song that leads many to fear and trust the LORD
It remains a secret that no one hears
It teaches people to trust themselves alone
challenge.explanation: The new song of praise causes many to see, fear, and trust in the LORD.
challenge.q: How does personal deliverance become a witness to others?

paragraphs.title: God’s Wonders and Gratitude Beyond Sacrifices

answers: The LORD’s many wonderful works and thoughts
The power of his enemies
The wealth of mankind
easy.explanation: He speaks of the LORD’s wonderful works and thoughts, which cannot be numbered.
easy.q: What does the speaker marvel at?

answers: Sacrifice and offering
A new song
Faithfulness and truth
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire,” and that burnt and sin offerings were not required.
easy.q: What did the LORD not desire or require as the speaker’s only response?

answers: Within his heart
Outside the congregation
Only upon his lips
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “thy law is within my heart.”
easy.q: Where does the speaker say God’s law is?

answers: A willingness to hear and obey God
That the speaker’s ears were covered
A command to remain silent
medium.explanation: The opened ears represent attentiveness to God’s will rather than reliance on ritual alone.
medium.q: What does “mine ears hast thou opened” emphasize?

answers: By doing God’s will and proclaiming His righteousness
By hiding his faith and remaining silent
By trusting in his own strength
medium.explanation: He delights to do God’s will and preaches righteousness in the great congregation.
medium.q: How does the speaker express his gratitude?

answers: He refuses to hide God’s righteousness, faithfulness, salvation, and lovingkindness
He wants to conceal his faith
He wants to replace God’s law
medium.explanation: He says he has not hidden God’s righteousness or concealed His lovingkindness and truth.
medium.q: Why does the speaker proclaim God’s righteousness in the great congregation?

answers: True gratitude includes listening to and doing God’s will
True gratitude removes the need to listen
True gratitude depends only on sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The speaker’s opened ears, delight in God’s will, and inward law all show obedient gratitude.
challenge.q: What is the connection between hearing God’s will and offering true gratitude?

answers: God’s instruction has become an inward part of the speaker’s life
The speaker has hidden God’s law from everyone
The speaker does not recognize God’s law
challenge.explanation: The law is internalized in his heart, while he openly proclaims God’s righteousness and truth.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the law being “within my heart”?

answers: Listening to God, doing His will, and proclaiming His righteousness
Hiding, remaining silent, and avoiding the congregation
Offering sacrifices, boasting, and forgetting mercy
challenge.explanation: The passage joins opened ears, delight in God’s will, and public proclamation.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the speaker’s way of giving thanks?

paragraphs.title: A Renewed Plea from Within Distress

answers: Deliver and help him
Hide His righteousness
Give him riches
easy.explanation: He asks, “Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me” and, “make haste to help me.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?

answers: That they be ashamed and confounded
That they rejoice with him
That they teach him wisdom
easy.explanation: He asks that those seeking his soul be driven backward and put to shame.
easy.q: What does the speaker ask to happen to those seeking his soul?

answers: Poor and needy
Rich and powerful
A king and warrior
easy.explanation: The final verse begins, “But I am poor and needy.”
easy.q: How does the speaker describe himself at the end?

answers: Innumerable evils surround him, his iniquities have taken hold of him, and his heart fails
He wants to praise his enemies
He believes he needs no help
medium.explanation: He describes overwhelming evils, iniquities, inability to look up, and a failing heart.
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask the LORD to make haste to help him?

answers: His courage and strength have failed
His heart is filled with celebration
His heart is eager to sing
medium.explanation: The phrase follows the description of overwhelming troubles and expresses deep weakness.
medium.q: What does “my heart faileth me” mean in context?

answers: Those who seek the LORD and love His salvation
Those who wish him evil
Those who turn aside to lies
medium.explanation: He asks that those who seek the LORD rejoice and say continually, “The LORD be magnified.”
medium.q: For whom does the speaker ask that there be rejoicing?

answers: The speaker is in great distress but continues to depend on the LORD
The speaker is carefree and asks for nothing
The speaker trusts only in his own strength
challenge.explanation: Although he describes evils, iniquities, and weakness, he still calls the LORD his help and deliverer.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in this part of the psalm?

answers: He asks shame for his enemies but joy and praise for those who seek God
He asks the same thing for both groups
He asks joy for his enemies and shame for those who seek God
challenge.explanation: Those wishing him evil should be put to shame, while those who seek God should rejoice and magnify the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the speaker’s request concerning God’s seekers differ from his request concerning his enemies?

answers: He acknowledges his dependence on God, calling Him his help and deliverer
He believes he needs no help
He credits his enemies for delivering him
challenge.explanation: Though poor and needy, he declares, “thou art my help and my deliverer.”
challenge.q: What does the ending reveal about the speaker’s attitude toward God’s help?
